claim: TNF regulates numerous important biological processes including inflammation and cell death.
source: The apical inflammatory cytokine TNF regulates numerous important biological processes including inflammation and cell death, and drives inflammatory diseases.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract as established knowledge about TNF function.

claim: TNF drives inflammatory diseases.
source: The apical inflammatory cytokine TNF regulates numerous important biological processes including inflammation and cell death, and drives inflammatory diseases.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract as established knowledge about TNF's role in disease.

claim: TNF secretion requires TACE (also called ADAM17).
source: TNF secretion requires TACE (also called ADAM17), which cleaves TNF from its transmembrane tether.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract as established knowledge about the mechanism of TNF secretion.

claim: TACE cleaves TNF from its transmembrane tether.
source: TNF secretion requires TACE (also called ADAM17), which cleaves TNF from its transmembrane tether.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract as established knowledge about TACE's proteolytic function.

claim: The trafficking of TACE to the cell surface depends on membrane proteins called iRhoms.
source: The trafficking of TACE to the cell surface, and stimulation of its proteolytic activity, depends on membrane proteins, called iRhoms.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract as established knowledge about TACE regulation.

claim: The stimulation of TACE's proteolytic activity depends on membrane proteins called iRhoms.
source: The trafficking of TACE to the cell surface, and stimulation of its proteolytic activity, depends on membrane proteins, called iRhoms.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract as established knowledge about TACE regulation.

claim: An immunoprecipitation/mass spectrometry screen was performed to identify iRhom-binding proteins.
source: To delineate how the TNF/TACE/iRhom axis is regulated, we performed an immunoprecipitation/mass spectrometry screen to identify iRhom-binding proteins.
evidence: This describes the experimental approach used in the study.

claim: The immunoprecipitation/mass spectrometry screen identified a novel protein named iTAP (iRhom Tail-Associated Protein).
source: This identified a novel protein, that we name iTAP (iRhom Tail-Associated Protein) that binds to iRhoms, enhancing the cell surface stability of iRhoms and TACE, preventing their degradation in lysosomes.
evidence: This is a primary finding from the mass spectrometry screen described in the abstract.

claim: iTAP binds to iRhoms.
source: This identified a novel protein, that we name iTAP (iRhom Tail-Associated Protein) that binds to iRhoms, enhancing the cell surface stability of iRhoms and TACE, preventing their degradation in lysosomes.
evidence: This is a primary finding from the study described in the abstract.

claim: iTAP enhances the cell surface stability of iRhoms and TACE.
source: This identified a novel protein, that we name iTAP (iRhom Tail-Associated Protein) that binds to iRhoms, enhancing the cell surface stability of iRhoms and TACE, preventing their degradation in lysosomes.
evidence: This is a primary finding from the study described in the abstract.

claim: iTAP prevents degradation of iRhoms and TACE in lysosomes.
source: This identified a novel protein, that we name iTAP (iRhom Tail-Associated Protein) that binds to iRhoms, enhancing the cell surface stability of iRhoms and TACE, preventing their degradation in lysosomes.
evidence: This is a primary finding from the study described in the abstract.

claim: Depleting iTAP in primary human macrophages profoundly impaired TNF production.
source: Depleting iTAP in primary human macrophages profoundly impaired TNF production and tissues from iTAP KO mice exhibit a pronounced depletion in active TACE levels.
evidence: This is a primary finding from experiments with primary human macrophages described in the abstract.

claim: Tissues from iTAP KO mice exhibit a pronounced depletion in active TACE levels.
source: Depleting iTAP in primary human macrophages profoundly impaired TNF production and tissues from iTAP KO mice exhibit a pronounced depletion in active TACE levels.
evidence: This is a primary finding from experiments with iTAP knockout mice described in the abstract.

claim: iTAP is a physiological regulator of TNF signalling.
source: Our work identifies iTAP as a physiological regulator of TNF signalling and a novel target for the control of inflammation.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the experimental findings described in the abstract.

claim: iTAP is a novel target for the control of inflammation.
source: Our work identifies iTAP as a physiological regulator of TNF signalling and a novel target for the control of inflammation.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the experimental findings described in the abstract.

claim: TNF controls numerous important biological processes including inflammation, fever, apoptosis, necroptosis, cachexia, tumorigenesis, viral infection, and insulin signaling.
source: The cytokine TNF controls numerous important biological processes (e.g. inflammation, fever, apoptosis, necroptosis, cachexia, tumorigenesis, viral infection, insulin signaling) and is heavily implicated in inflammatory disease (Brenner et al., 2015).
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge with citation support.

claim: TNF is heavily implicated in inflammatory disease.
source: The cytokine TNF controls numerous important biological processes (e.g. inflammation, fever, apoptosis, necroptosis, cachexia, tumorigenesis, viral infection, insulin signaling) and is heavily implicated in inflammatory disease (Brenner et al., 2015).
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge with citation support.

claim: Anti-TNF biologics are the highest-selling drugs internationally.
source: Anti-TNF biologics are the highest-selling drugs internationally and there is intense interest in how TNF signaling is regulated (Brenner et al., 2015).
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge with citation support.

claim: TNF is expressed by a range of cells including macrophages, lymphocytes, natural killer cells, endothelial cells and microglia.
source: TNF is expressed by a range of cells including macrophages, lymphocytes, natural killer cells, endothelial cells and microglia and is synthesized as a type II transmembrane protein with a cytosolic domain of 76 amino acids that assembles into a trimer (Locksley et al., 2001).
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge with citation support.

claim: TNF is synthesized as a type II transmembrane protein with a cytosolic domain of 76 amino acids that assembles into a trimer.
source: TNF is expressed by a range of cells including macrophages, lymphocytes, natural killer cells, endothelial cells and microglia and is synthesized as a type II transmembrane protein with a cytosolic domain of 76 amino acids that assembles into a trimer (Locksley et al., 2001).
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge with citation support.

claim: TNF can activate two distinct receptors.
source: The capacity of TNF to trigger such pleiotropic biological outcomes is determined by its ability to activate two distinct receptors (Locksley et al., 2001).
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge with citation support.

claim: TNFRI activation is generally associated with induction of acute or chronic inflammatory responses, or cell death.
source: Generally, TNFRI activation is associated with induction of acute or chronic inflammatory responses, or cell death, whereas TNFRII mediates pro-survival signals and has been associated with the tolerogenic properties of regulatory T cells (Kleijwegt et al., 2010; Richter et al., 2012).
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge with citation support.

claim: TNFRII mediates pro-survival signals and has been associated with the tolerogenic properties of regulatory T cells.
source: Generally, TNFRI activation is associated with induction of acute or chronic inflammatory responses, or cell death, whereas TNFRII mediates pro-survival signals and has been associated with the tolerogenic properties of regulatory T cells (Kleijwegt et al., 2010; Richter et al., 2012).
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge with citation support.

claim: The transmembrane form of TNF (mTNF) triggers juxtacrine signalling.
source: The transmembrane form of TNF (mTNF) triggers juxtacrine signalling, while TNF released as a soluble form (sTNF), drives paracrine signalling.
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge about TNF signaling mechanisms.

claim: TNF released as a soluble form (sTNF) drives paracrine signalling.
source: The transmembrane form of TNF (mTNF) triggers juxtacrine signalling, while TNF released as a soluble form (sTNF), drives paracrine signalling.
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge about TNF signaling mechanisms.

claim: TNFRI can be activated by both soluble and membrane TNF.
source: Notably, whereas TNFRI can be activated by both soluble and membrane TNF, TNFRII is activated efficiently only by mTNF (Grell et al., 1995).
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge with citation support.

claim: TNFRII is activated efficiently only by mTNF.
source: Notably, whereas TNFRI can be activated by both soluble and membrane TNF, TNFRII is activated efficiently only by mTNF (Grell et al., 1995).
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge with citation support.

claim: mTNF is sufficient for the development and maintenance of some lymphoid tissues.
source: Whereas mTNF is sufficient for the development and maintenance of some lymphoid tissues, soluble TNF is important for acute and chronic inflammation.
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge about the differential roles of TNF forms.

claim: Soluble TNF is important for acute and chronic inflammation.
source: Whereas mTNF is sufficient for the development and maintenance of some lymphoid tissues, soluble TNF is important for acute and chronic inflammation.
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge about the differential roles of TNF forms.

claim: Mice unable to produce soluble TNF resist endotoxic shock.
source: Specifically, mice unable to produce soluble TNF resist endotoxic shock and exhibit reduced severity in experimental autoimmune encephalomyelitis models (Ruuls et al., 2001).
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge with citation support.

claim: Mice unable to produce soluble TNF exhibit reduced severity in experimental autoimmune encephalomyelitis models.
source: Specifically, mice unable to produce soluble TNF resist endotoxic shock and exhibit reduced severity in experimental autoimmune encephalomyelitis models (Ruuls et al., 2001).
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge with citation support.

claim: Membrane TNF is insufficient to rescue the defects in primary B cell follicle formation observed in TNF KO mice.
source: Membrane TNF is also insufficient to rescue the defects in primary B cell follicle formation observed in TNF KO mice, but mediates protective immune responses to intracellular bacterial infection (Ruuls et al., 2001; Alexopoulou et al., 2006).
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge with citation support.

claim: Membrane TNF mediates protective immune responses to intracellular bacterial infection.
source: Membrane TNF is also insufficient to rescue the defects in primary B cell follicle formation observed in TNF KO mice, but mediates protective immune responses to intracellular bacterial infection (Ruuls et al., 2001; Alexopoulou et al., 2006).
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge with citation support.

claim: The release of soluble TNF from the cell surface is catalyzed by the protease TACE.
source: This is catalyzed by the protease TACE (TNF α Converting Enzyme) (Horiuchi et al., 2007; Peschon et al., 1998), also called ADAM17 (A Disintegrin And Metalloprotease) (Gooz, 2010; Zunke and Rose-John, 2017).
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge with citation support.

claim: TACE is also called ADAM17.
source: This is catalyzed by the protease TACE (TNF α Converting Enzyme) (Horiuchi et al., 2007; Peschon et al., 1998), also called ADAM17 (A Disintegrin And Metalloprotease) (Gooz, 2010; Zunke and Rose-John, 2017).
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge with citation support.

claim: TACE cleaves both TNF and TNF receptors.
source: Crucially, TACE imposes an additional layer of versatility and regulation to TNF signaling, since in addition to cleaving TNF, both TNFRs are also physiological TACE substrates.
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge about TACE's substrate specificity.

claim: TACE is a master orchestrator of TNF signaling.
source: Hence, TACE is a master orchestrator of TNF signaling, tuning signaling to fit a panoply of biological roles ranging from inflammatory responses to immune tolerance.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from established knowledge about TACE's multiple roles.

claim: TACE cleaves activating ligands of the EGFR.
source: TACE also has significant biological importance beyond TNF signaling since it cleaves other prominent substrates, including the activating ligands of the EGFR (Epidermal Growth Factor Receptor), an important pathway that drives growth control, tissue repair and immune responses.
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge about TACE's substrate specificity.

claim: TACE is stringently regulated.
source: Given its ability to elicit potent biological responses, it is unsurprising that TACE is stringently regulated (Murphy, 2009; Grötzinger et al., 2017).
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge with citation support.

claim: A major control point in TACE regulation involves its trafficking within the secretory pathway.
source: A major control point in TACE regulation involves its trafficking within the secretory pathway (Schlöndorff et al., 2000).
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge with citation support.

claim: TACE is synthesized in the endoplasmic reticulum (ER) as a catalytically inactive precursor.
source: TACE is synthesized in the endoplasmic reticulum (ER) as a catalytically inactive precursor.
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge about TACE biosynthesis.

claim: TACE becomes proteolytically active through removal of its prodomain by proprotein convertases in the trans-Golgi.
source: For TACE to become proteolytically active, it must undergo a maturation step—removal of its prodomain—which is catalysed by proprotein convertases in the trans-Golgi (Schlöndorff et al., 2000).
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge with citation support.

claim: The exit of TACE from the ER and its trafficking to the cell surface requires regulatory proteins called iRhoms.
source: The exit of TACE from the ER and its trafficking to the cell surface requires regulatory proteins called iRhoms (Adrain et al., 2012; McIlwain et al., 2012; Li et al., 2015).
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge with citation support.

claim: iRhom KO mice or cells in which iRhoms are ablated lack TACE activity.
source: Hence, iRhom KO mice, or cells in which iRhoms are ablated, lack TACE activity (Adrain et al., 2012; Li et al., 2015; Christova et al., 2013).
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge with citation support.

claim: Mice null for iRhom2 cannot secrete TNF.
source: Mice null for iRhom2, whose expression is enriched in myeloid cells, cannot secrete TNF (Adrain et al., 2012; McIlwain et al., 2012; Siggs et al., 2012).
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge with citation support.

claim: iRhom2 expression is enriched in myeloid cells.
source: Mice null for iRhom2, whose expression is enriched in myeloid cells, cannot secrete TNF (Adrain et al., 2012; McIlwain et al., 2012; Siggs et al., 2012).
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge with citation support.

claim: TACE activity is stimulated on the cell surface by agents including phorbol esters, Toll-like receptor agonists and G-protein coupled receptor ligands.
source: An important checkpoint to license TACE activity involves its stimulation on the cell surface by agents including phorbol esters, Toll-like receptor agonists and G-protein coupled receptor ligands (Grötzinger et al., 2017; Arribas et al., 1996; Hall and Blobel, 2012; Brandl et al., 2010; Wetzker and Böhmer, 2003).
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge with citation support.

claim: iRhoms exist in a molecular assembly with TACE on the cell surface called the 'sheddase complex'.
source: Importantly, as well as controlling TACE trafficking, iRhoms exist in a molecular assembly with TACE on the cell surface—the 'sheddase complex' which is central to stimulation of TACE sheddase activity.
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge about the iRhom-TACE complex.

claim: Within the sheddase complex, iRhom proteins serve as a platform that senses and transduces TACE-activating stimuli.
source: Within the sheddase complex, iRhom proteins serve as a platform that senses and transduces TACE-activating stimuli.
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge about iRhom function.

claim: TACE-activating agents provoke MAP kinase-dependent phosphorylation of the iRhom2 cytoplasmic tail.
source: These agents provoke the MAP kinase-dependent phosphorylation of the iRhom2 cytoplasmic tail, which in turn triggers the recruitment of 14-3-3 proteins.
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge about the mechanism of TACE activation.

claim: Phosphorylation of the iRhom2 cytoplasmic tail triggers the recruitment of 14-3-3 proteins.
source: These agents provoke the MAP kinase-dependent phosphorylation of the iRhom2 cytoplasmic tail, which in turn triggers the recruitment of 14-3-3 proteins.
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge about the mechanism of TACE activation.

claim: Recruitment of 14-3-3 proteins enforces the detachment of TACE from iRhom2 or triggers a conformational change within the sheddase complex.
source: This enforces the detachment of TACE from iRhom2 (or triggers a conformational change within the sheddase complex) which is required to facilitate TACE's ability to cleave its substrates, including TNF (Grieve et al., 2017; Cavadas et al., 2017).
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge with citation support.

claim: iRhoms are allosteric regulators of TACE's proteolytic activity as well as acting as trafficking factors.
source: Hence, iRhoms are allosteric regulators of TACE's proteolytic activity as well as acting as trafficking factors.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from established knowledge about iRhom function.

claim: PACS-2 is a protein that colocalizes with mature TACE in endocytic compartments.
source: An exception is PACS-2 (Phosphofurin Acidic Cluster Sorting Protein 2), a protein that colocalizes with mature TACE in endocytic compartments (Dombernowsky et al., 2015) and controls its endocytic recycling.
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge with citation support.

claim: PACS-2 controls TACE's endocytic recycling.
source: An exception is PACS-2 (Phosphofurin Acidic Cluster Sorting Protein 2), a protein that colocalizes with mature TACE in endocytic compartments (Dombernowsky et al., 2015) and controls its endocytic recycling.
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge with citation support.

claim: Ablation of PACS-2 in cells impairs the cell surface availability of TACE, reducing substrate cleavage.
source: Ablation of PACS-2 in cells impairs the cell surface availability of TACE, reducing substrate cleavage (Dombernowsky et al., 2015).
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge with citation support.

claim: PACS-2 has a relatively modest impact on TACE biology in vivo.
source: However, PACS-2 has a relatively modest impact on TACE biology in vivo (Dombernowsky et al., 2017), suggesting the possibility of unidentified trafficking regulators that may act separately from, or redundantly with, PACS-2.
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge with citation support.

claim: TACE is endocytosed and degraded in lysosomes.
source: It has been shown that not only TACE (Doedens and Black, 2000; Lorenzen et al., 2016), but also iRhoms (Grieve et al., 2017; Cavadas et al., 2017) are endocytosed and degraded in lysosomes, but the machinery involved in maintaining stable cell surface levels of the sheddase complex is unknown.
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge with citation support.

claim: iRhoms are endocytosed and degraded in lysosomes.
source: It has been shown that not only TACE (Doedens and Black, 2000; Lorenzen et al., 2016), but also iRhoms (Grieve et al., 2017; Cavadas et al., 2017) are endocytosed and degraded in lysosomes, but the machinery involved in maintaining stable cell surface levels of the sheddase complex is unknown.
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge with citation support.

claim: Ablation of iTAP triggers the mis-sorting of iRhom2 and TACE to lysosomes, where they are degraded.
source: Ablation of iTAP triggers the mis-sorting of iRhom2, and consequently, TACE, to lysosomes, where they are degraded.
evidence: This is a primary finding from the study described in the introduction.

claim: Loss of iTAP results in a dramatic reduction in TACE activity and TNF secretion.
source: Consistent with this, loss of iTAP results in a dramatic reduction in TACE activity and TNF secretion.
evidence: This is a primary finding from the study described in the introduction.

claim: iTAP is essential for the control of the stability of iRhom2 and TACE on the plasma membrane.
source: Here we identify a novel protein that we name iTAP (iRhom Tail-Associated Protein) that is essential for the control of the stability of iRhom2 and TACE on the plasma membrane.
evidence: This is a primary conclusion from the study described in the introduction.

claim: A panel of HEK 293ET cell lines stably expressing HA-tagged forms of full-length iRhom1, iRhom2, or the iRhom1 N-terminal cytoplasmic tail only was generated.
source: As shown in Figure 1A, we generated a panel of HEK 293ET cell lines stably expressing HA-tagged forms of full-length iRhom1, iRhom2, or the iRhom1 N-terminal cytoplasmic tail only.
evidence: This describes the experimental approach used in the study.

claim: Rhbdd2, RHBDD3, and Ubac2 were included as specificity controls in the immunoprecipitation experiments.
source: To focus only on proteins that bind selectively to iRhoms, we included the related rhomboid-like proteins, Rhbdd2, RHBDD3, Ubac2, as specificity controls (Figure 1A).
evidence: This describes the experimental design used in the study.

claim: Only immunoprecipitates from cells expressing full-length HA-tagged iRhom1 or iRhom2 captured endogenous TACE.
source: As expected, only immunoprecipitates (IPs) from cells expressing full-length HA-tagged iRhom1 or iRhom2 captured endogenous TACE, confirming the validity of the approach (Figure 1B).
evidence: This is a finding from the immunoprecipitation experiments shown in Figure 1B.

claim: Mass spectrometry analysis revealed peptides from FRMD8 in IPs of iRhom1 or iRhom2, but not in control IPs.
source: This analysis revealed, in multiple replicate experiments, peptides from a largely uncharacterized protein, called FRMD8 (FERM Domain-containing protein 8), in IPs of iRhom1 or iRhom2, but not in control IPs of Rhbdd2, RHBDD3 and Ubac2 (Figure 1C).
evidence: This is a primary finding from the mass spectrometry experiments shown in Figure 1C.

claim: FRMD8 was found in IPs from cells expressing the N-terminus of iRhom1.
source: Furthermore, FRMD8 was found in IPs from cells expressing the N-terminus of iRhom1 (Figure 1A,C), suggesting that it was recruited to the iRhom cytoplasmic tail (R-domain), an important regulatory region (Grieve et al., 2017; Cavadas et al., 2017; Maney et al., 2015; Hosur et al., 2014).
evidence: This is a finding from the mass spectrometry experiments shown in Figure 1C.

claim: FRMD8 was named iTAP (iRhom Tail Associated Protein).
source: In light of this, we named the novel protein iTAP ('iRhom Tail Associated Protein').
evidence: This describes the naming of the newly identified protein.

claim: iTAP encodes a FERM (band 4.1/Ezrin/Radixin/Moesin) domain.
source: A closer inspection of the iTAP sequence revealed that it encodes a FERM (band 4.1/Ezrin/Radixin/Moesin) domain (Chishti et al., 1998) (Figure 1D).
evidence: This is a finding from sequence analysis shown in Figure 1D.

claim: Proteins containing FERM domains fulfil many important roles, including signaling, organization of the cell cortex and its mechanical properties and cell surface stabilization of membrane proteins or phospholipids.
source: Proteins containing FERM domains fulfil many important roles, including signaling, organization of the cell cortex and its mechanical properties and cell surface stabilization (anchoring) of membrane proteins or phospholipids (McClatchey, 2014; Fehon et al., 2010; Hoover and Bryant, 2000; Baines et al., 2014; Moleirinho et al., 2013).
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge with citation support.

claim: The well-characterized FERM domain contains three distinct lobes that together resemble a three-leaf clover.
source: The well-characterized FERM domain contains three distinct lobes that together resemble a three-leaf clover (Pearson et al., 2000).
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge with citation support.

claim: Unlike most FERM domain-containing proteins, iTAP contains only the central (FERM-M) lobe.
source: However, unlike most FERM domain-containing proteins, but similar to its paralog KRIT1—an adaptor protein in the cerebral cavernous malformation pathway that regulates the establishment of vasculature (Pal et al., 2017), iTAP contains only the central (FERM-M) lobe (Figure 1D).
evidence: This is a finding from sequence analysis shown in Figure 1D.

claim: iTAP orthologs are present in metazoans, including Drosophila and Danio.
source: iTAP orthologs are present in metazoans, including Drosophila and Danio (Kategaya et al., 2009).
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge with citation support.

claim: The iTAP protein is expressed broadly and is co-expressed with TACE and iRhom1 or iRhom2 in a range of tissues relevant for TACE biology.
source: The iTAP protein is expressed broadly and is co-expressed with TACE and iRhom1 or iRhom2 in a range of tissues relevant for TACE biology (Figure 1—figure supplement 1A,B).
evidence: This is a finding from expression analysis shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1A,B.

claim: Independent immunoprecipitation experiments verified that iTAP binds specifically to both iRhom1 and iRhom2, but not to the related rhomboid pseudoproteases Ubac2 and Rhbdd2.
source: Independent immunoprecipitation experiments verified that iTAP binds specifically to both iRhom1 and iRhom2, but not to the related rhomboid pseudoproteases Ubac2 and Rhbdd2 (Figure 2A).
evidence: This is a finding from immunoprecipitation experiments shown in Figure 2A.

claim: iTAP binds the cytoplasmic tail of iRhoms.
source: iTAP binds the cytoplasmic tail of iRhoms, since a mutant containing only the cytoplasmic tail of iRhom1 bound iTAP robustly, whereas a mutant lacking all of the iRhom2 cytoplasmic tail (∆Nterm) failed to bind (Figure 2A).
evidence: This is a finding from immunoprecipitation experiments shown in Figure 2A.

claim: Removal of the iRhom homology domain (IRHD) from iRhom2 had no impact on iTAP recruitment.
source: By contrast, removal of the iRhom homology domain (IRHD), the luminal globular domain between transmembrane helices 1 and 2 (Figure 2B) from iRhom2 had no impact on iTAP recruitment (Figure 2A).
evidence: This is a finding from immunoprecipitation experiments shown in Figure 2A.

claim: When iTAP-FLAG was immunoprecipitated from cell lysates, endogenous iRhom1 and iRhom2 were detected.
source: Notably, when iTAP-FLAG, but not a panel of control proteins, was immunoprecipitated from cell lysates, we detected the binding of endogenous iRhom1 and iRhom2 to iTAP (Table 1).
evidence: This is a finding from immunoprecipitation experiments shown in Table 1.

claim: iTAP is a specific endogenous interactor of both iRhom paralogs in mammals.
source: These data confirm that iTAP is a specific endogenous interactor of both iRhom paralogs in mammals.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the immunoprecipitation data.

claim: Amino acids 191–271 of the iRhom2 tail contain the main determinant for iTAP binding.
source: This revealed that amino acids 191–271 of the iRhom2 tail contain the main determinant for iTAP binding (Figure 2C,D).
evidence: This is a finding from deletion mapping experiments shown in Figure 2C,D.

claim: iTAP-GFP exhibited a powdery staining in the cytoplasm and nucleus when examined in fixed and permeabilized mammalian cells.
source: As shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1A, iTAP-GFP exhibited a powdery staining in the cytoplasm and nucleus.
evidence: This is a finding from microscopy experiments shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1A.

claim: When co-expressed with mCherry-tagged iRhom2, iTAP was recruited to areas of iRhom2 staining.
source: When co-expressed with mCherry-tagged iRhom2, iTAP was recruited to areas of iRhom2 staining (Figure 2—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: This is a finding from microscopy experiments shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1B.

claim: iTAP was ablated in HEK 293ET cells using CRISPR.
source: To determine the functional importance of iTAP binding to iRhom, we used CRISPR to ablate iTAP in HEK 293ET cells, which was confirmed by the lack of iTAP protein expression (Figure 3A).
evidence: This describes the experimental approach used in the study, shown in Figure 3A.

claim: The PMA-induced shedding of a panel of chimeric alkaline phosphatase (AP) TACE substrates was substantially impaired in iTAP KO cells.
source: Notably, the PMA-induced shedding of a panel of chimeric alkaline phosphatase (AP) TACE substrates (Sahin et al., 2004), including EGFR ligands and TNF, was substantially impaired in iTAP KO cells (Figure 3B).
evidence: This is a primary finding from shedding assays shown in Figure 3B.

claim: The shedding defect in iTAP KO cells was rescued by the expression of an iTAP cDNA.
source: This shedding defect was rescued by the expression of an iTAP cDNA, confirming that the loss of iTAP was directly responsible for defective TACE activity (Figure 3C,D).
evidence: This is a finding from rescue experiments shown in Figure 3C,D.

claim: TACE immunoprecipitates from iTAP KO cells exhibited substantially depleted levels of TACE activity.
source: As expected, TACE immunoprecipitates (Figure 3—figure supplement 1A) from iTAP KO cells exhibited substantially depleted levels of TACE activity (Figure 3—figure supplement 1B), confirming that the loss of iTAP specifically impairs TACE rather than affecting its substrates.
evidence: This is a finding from TACE activity assays shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1B.

claim: The cleavage of ADAM10 substrates EGF and BTC was unaffected by loss of iTAP.
source: Notably the cleavage of these ADAM10 substrates was unaffected (Figure 3E) while the release of a model secreted substrate was similarly unimpaired in iTAP KO cells (Figure 3F).
evidence: This is a finding from shedding assays shown in Figure 3E.

claim: The release of a model secreted substrate was unimpaired in iTAP KO cells.
source: Notably the cleavage of these ADAM10 substrates was unaffected (Figure 3E) while the release of a model secreted substrate was similarly unimpaired in iTAP KO cells (Figure 3F).
evidence: This is a finding from secretion assays shown in Figure 3F.

claim: iTAP is a highly specific regulator of the TACE pathway that does not affect secretion in general.
source: These data confirm that iTAP is a highly specific regulator of the TACE pathway that does not affect secretion in general.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the shedding and secretion assay data.

claim: iTAP KO cell lines were dramatically depleted of mature TACE.
source: Although a few experiments showed an overall reduction in the TACE levels in iTAP KO cells, the consistent and most pronounced phenotype, found in all iTAP-null cell lines, was a dramatic depletion of mature TACE, identified by its faster migration pattern (Figure 4B).
evidence: This is a primary finding from western blot analysis shown in Figure 4B.

claim: Deglycosylation analysis confirmed that iTAP KO cell lines were substantially depleted of mature TACE.
source: This confirmed that iTAP KO cell lines were substantially depleted of mature TACE (Figure 4B,D,E), which could be rescued specifically by iTAP overexpression in iTAP KO cells (Figure 4E).
evidence: This is a finding from deglycosylation experiments shown in Figure 4B,D,E.

claim: The loss of mature TACE in iTAP KO cells could be rescued specifically by iTAP overexpression.
source: This confirmed that iTAP KO cell lines were substantially depleted of mature TACE (Figure 4B,D,E), which could be rescued specifically by iTAP overexpression in iTAP KO cells (Figure 4E).
evidence: This is a finding from rescue experiments shown in Figure 4E.

claim: Overexpression of iTAP in WT cells modestly enhanced mature TACE levels.
source: Overexpression of iTAP in WT cells also modestly enhanced mature TACE levels (Figure 4E) and densitometric analysis confirmed once again that the loss, or reintroduction, of iTAP most profoundly affected mature TACE levels (Figure 4E, graphs).
evidence: This is a finding from overexpression experiments shown in Figure 4E.

claim: iTAP-null cells lack mature, cell surface TACE.
source: We tested this hypothesis in experiments with a non-cell permeable biotinylated cross-linker, which revealed drastically reduced mature TACE levels on the cell surface (Figure 4F).
evidence: This is a finding from cell surface biotinylation experiments shown in Figure 4F.

claim: The maturation of other related ADAM proteases was unimpaired by loss of iTAP.
source: Finally, as predicted by stringent specificity of iTAP for TACE, the maturation of other related ADAM proteases was unimpaired (Figure 4G).
evidence: This is a finding from western blot analysis shown in Figure 4G.

claim: Endogenous iRhom2 was depleted in iTAP KO RAW 264.7 cells.
source: Strikingly, endogenous iRhom2 was depleted in iTAP KO RAW 264.7 cells (Figure 5A), indicating that iTAP is essential to maintain iRhom2 stability.
evidence: This is a primary finding from western blot analysis shown in Figure 5A.

claim: iTAP is essential to maintain iRhom2 stability.
source: Strikingly, endogenous iRhom2 was depleted in iTAP KO RAW 264.7 cells (Figure 5A), indicating that iTAP is essential to maintain iRhom2 stability.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the western blot data in Figure 5A.

claim: iTAP transient overexpression increased steady state levels of overexpressed iRhom2-HA and enhanced the half-life of the protein during cycloheximide treatment.
source: Consistent with this, in HEK 293ET cells, iTAP transient overexpression increased steady state levels of overexpressed iRhom2-HA and enhanced the half-life (see graph, Figure 5B) of the protein, during a timecourse of cycloheximide (CHX) treatment, used to block additional protein synthesis (Figure 5B).
evidence: This is a finding from cycloheximide chase experiments shown in Figure 5B.

claim: Transiently overexpressed iRhom2-HA was destabilized in iTAP KO cells.
source: As anticipated by these results, transiently overexpressed iRhom2-HA was also destabilized in iTAP KO cells (Figure 5—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: This is a finding from experiments shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 1A.

claim: There is striking colocalization between mCherry-iRhom2 and iTAP-GFP when they are co-expressed in HeLa cells.
source: Consistent with the ability of iTAP to impact profoundly on iRhom2 stability, we observed striking colocalization between mCherry-iRhom2 and iTAP-GFP, when they were co-expressed in HeLa cells, as judged by Pearson's correlation and Manders' overlap coefficients (Figure 5C).
evidence: This is a finding from microscopy experiments shown in Figure 5C.

claim: iTAP expression selectively enriched the post-ER fraction of iRhom2.
source: Strikingly, the co-expression of iTAP increased the overall levels of iRhom2, but selectively enriched the post-ER fraction of iRhom2 (Figure 5D), suggesting a disproportionate impact on the form of iRhom2 that had traversed to the late secretory pathway.
evidence: This is a finding from deglycosylation experiments shown in Figure 5D.

claim: iTAP IPs from cross-linked cells showed a clear enrichment for post-ER (Endo-H insensitive) iRhom2.
source: Notably, compared to IPs done without cross-linking, iTAP IPs from cross-linked cells showed a clear enrichment for post-ER (Endo-H insensitive) iRhom2 (Figure 5E), although the ER-localized form of iRhom2 was also readily detected.
evidence: This is a finding from cross-linking and immunoprecipitation experiments shown in Figure 5E.

claim: The loading of iTAP onto the sheddase complex occurs already in the ER but the binding is sustained throughout the sheddase complex's itinerary in the late secretory pathway.
source: Taken together with the colocalization data (Figure 5C), we propose that the loading of iTAP onto the sheddase complex occurs already in the ER but the binding is sustained throughout the sheddase complex's itinerary in the late secretory pathway, where iTAP's affinity for iRhom2 appears to be higher.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the cross-linking and colocalization data.

claim: The ER exit of iRhom2 was unimpaired in iTAP KO cells.
source: Finally, ruling out a requirement for iTAP in controlling the ER-to-Golgi trafficking of iRhom2, we found that the ER exit of iRhom2 was unimpaired in iTAP KO cells, judged by the presence of Endo-H-resistant iRhom2 (Figure 5F; Figure 5—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: This is a finding from deglycosylation experiments shown in Figure 5F and Figure 5—figure supplement 1B.

claim: iTAP expression increased the steady state levels of cell surface iRhom2 and prolonged its cell surface stability during cycloheximide treatment.
source: Consistent with this premise, cell surface biotinylation experiments revealed that iTAP expression increased the steady state levels of cell surface iRhom2, and prolonged its cell surface stability, when CHX was used to block additional protein synthesis (Figure 5G).
evidence: This is a finding from cell surface biotinylation experiments shown in Figure 5G.

claim: The co-expression of iTAP with GFP-iRhom2 in MEFs enhanced the amount of GFP-iRhom2 detected on the plasma membrane.
source: In further agreement, the co-expression of iTAP with GFP-iRhom2 in MEFs enhanced the amount of GFP-iRhom2 detected on the plasma membrane (Figure 5H), supporting the premise that iTAP promotes the cell surface stability of iRhom2.
evidence: This is a finding from microscopy experiments shown in Figure 5H.

claim: iTAP's primary function is to stabilize the sheddase complex on the cell surface.
source: Together, our data indicate that iTAP's primary function is to stabilize the sheddase complex on the cell surface, reconciling the pronounced loss of mature TACE in iTAP KO cells and the increased binding propensity of iTAP for post-ER iRhom2.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the experimental findings.

claim: In WT HeLa cells, mCherry-iRhom2 did not co-stain appreciably with lysosomes.
source: As shown in Figure 6A, in WT HeLa cells, mCherry-iRhom2 did not co-stain appreciably with lysosomes.
evidence: This is a finding from microscopy experiments shown in Figure 6A.

claim: iTAP ablation resulted in a pronounced co-localization of iRhom2 with the lysosomal marker LAMP2.
source: By sharp contrast, iTAP ablation resulted in a pronounced co-localization of iRhom2 with the lysosomal marker LAMP2 (Lysosomal-Associated Membrane Protein 2), indicating mis-sorting of iRhom2 to lysosomes.
evidence: This is a primary finding from microscopy experiments shown in Figure 6A.

claim: The co-transfection of iTAP-GFP into iTAP KO HeLas rescued the aberrant accumulation of mCherry-iRhom2 in lysosomes.
source: This phenotype was specific since the co-transfection of iTAP-GFP into iTAP KO HeLas rescued the aberrant accumulation of mCherry-iRhom2 in lysosomes (Figure 6B), resulting in the marked co-localization of iRhom and iTAP observed previously (Figure 2—figure supplement 1B; Figure 5C).
evidence: This is a finding from rescue experiments shown in Figure 6B.

claim: A panel of lysosomotropic drugs that inhibit lysosomal proteolysis rescued iRhom2 stability in iTAP KO cells.
source: Consistent with these observations, a panel of lysosomotropic drugs that inhibit lysosomal proteolysis by impairing lysosomal acidification, rescued iRhom2 stability in iTAP KO cells (Figure 6C).
evidence: This is a finding from drug treatment experiments shown in Figure 6C.

claim: Overexpressed TACE-GFP was only recruited into lysosomes when sufficient iRhom2 was co-overexpressed.
source: Consistent with the notion that iRhom2 can influence the routing of TACE into lysosomes, we found that overexpressed TACE-GFP was only recruited into lysosomes when sufficient iRhom2 was co-overexpressed (Figure 6E).
evidence: This is a finding from microscopy experiments shown in Figure 6E.

claim: When the normal stoichiometric ratio of iTAP to iRhom2 is disrupted, iRhom2 is mis-sorted into the lysosome, then degraded.
source: In conclusion, our data reveal that when the normal stoichiometric ratio of iTAP to iRhom2 is disrupted (e.g. upon iRhom2 overexpression or iTAP ablation), iRhom2 is mis-sorted into the lysosome, then degraded.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the experimental findings.

claim: iTAP has an important physiological role in maintaining the cell surface stability of the iRhom2/TACE sheddase complex.
source: This highlights an important physiological role for iTAP in maintaining the cell surface stability of the iRhom2/TACE sheddase complex.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the experimental findings.

claim: iTAP is expressed in a range of mouse tissues relevant to iRhom and TACE biology.
source: iTAP is expressed in a range of mouse tissues relevant to iRhom and TACE biology (Peschon et al., 1998; Li et al., 2015) (Figure 1—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is a finding from expression analysis shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1.

claim: A mutant mouse was generated in which the first coding exon (exon 2) of the Frmd8 (iTAP) gene was deleted by CRISPR.
source: To examine the role of iTAP in mice, we generated a mutant in which the first coding exon (exon 2) of the Frmd8 (iTAP) gene was deleted by CRISPR (Figure 7A, Figure 7—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This describes the experimental approach used to generate iTAP knockout mice.

claim: MEFs isolated from iTAP KO embryos lacked iTAP protein expression.
source: MEFs isolated from iTAP KO embryos lacked iTAP protein expression, confirming the successful targeting of the Frmd8 gene (Figure 7B).
evidence: This is a finding from western blot analysis shown in Figure 7B.

claim: MEFs from two independent iTAP KO embryos exhibited the characteristic pronounced depletion of mature TACE levels.
source: As anticipated, MEFs from two independent iTAP KO embryos exhibited the characteristic pronounced depletion of mature TACE levels (Figure 7C).
evidence: This is a finding from western blot analysis shown in Figure 7C.

claim: A substantial depletion in the relative proportion of mature TACE was observed in a range of iTAP KO mouse tissues and in primary macrophages isolated from the bone marrow of iTAP KOs.
source: Significantly, with the possible exception of skin, where iTAP loss may be mitigated by other molecules, we observed a substantial depletion in the relative proportion of mature TACE in a range of iTAP KO mouse tissues, and in primary macrophages isolated from the bone marrow of iTAP KOs.
evidence: This is a primary finding from western blot analysis of mouse tissues.

claim: iTAP is an important physiological regulator of the iRhom/TACE/TNF axis in vivo.
source: These data reinforce the notion that iTAP is an important physiological regulator of the iRhom/TACE/TNF axis in vivo, making it important to dissect fully, in future, the organismal role of iTAP.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the mouse tissue data.

claim: The stimulated release of endogenous TNF in response to lipopolysaccharide in primary human macrophages was profoundly impaired when iTAP expression was ablated by specific siRNAs.
source: Notably, the stimulated release of endogenous TNF in response to lipopolysaccharide in these cells was profoundly impaired, when iTAP expression was ablated by specific siRNAs (Figure 7E).
evidence: This is a primary finding from ELISA experiments shown in Figure 7E.

claim: Secretion of IL-6 and IL-8, which is TACE-independent, was unaffected by iTAP depletion in primary human macrophages.
source: As expected, secretion of IL-6 and IL-8, which is TACE-independent, was unaffected (Figure 7E).
evidence: This is a finding from ELISA experiments shown in Figure 7E.

claim: iTAP is an essential physiological regulator of TNF secretion in primary human macrophages.
source: Our data indicate that iTAP is an essential physiological regulator of TNF secretion in primary human macrophages, the principal source of secreted TNF in vivo.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the primary human macrophage data.

claim: iTAP is essential to stabilize iRhom2 on the cell surface, preventing the routing of the sheddase complex to the lysosome.
source: We now show that iTAP is essential to stabilize iRhom2 on the cell surface, preventing the routing of the sheddase complex to the lysosome, and licensing TACE to cleave its substrates for signaling (summarized in Figure 8).
evidence: This is a summary conclusion from the study.

claim: iTAP emerges as an important regulator of inflammation and growth factor signaling, during development, normal physiology, infection and inflammatory disease.
source: iTAP, hence, emerges as an important regulator of inflammation and growth factor signaling, during development, normal physiology, infection and inflammatory disease.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the study's findings.

claim: FERM-domain proteins connect the cytoplasmic tails of cell surface client proteins to the cortical actin cytoskeleton to enhance their stability.
source: A general theme is that FERM-domain proteins connect the cytoplasmic tails of cell surface client proteins to the cortical actin cytoskeleton to enhance their stability (Hoover and Bryant, 2000; Baines et al., 2014; Moleirinho et al., 2013).
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge with citation support.

claim: Preliminary experiments failed to detect robust binding of iTAP to actin.
source: While iTAP binds to the cytoplasmic tails of iRhoms, which are found on the plasma membrane, our preliminary experiments failed to detect robust binding of iTAP to actin (Figure 8—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: This is a finding from preliminary experiments shown in Figure 8—figure supplement 1A.

claim: Loss of Snx17 results in a failure in endocytic recycling of β1 integrins, leading to their degradation in lysosomes.
source: Analogous to the degradation of iRhom2 in iTAP KO cells, loss of Snx17, which binds to the cytoplasmic tail of β1 integrins, results in a failure in their endocytic recycling, leading to their degradation in lysosomes (Böttcher et al., 2012).
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge with citation support.

claim: The iRhom2 cytoplasmic tail contains two motifs, NxxY and NPxY, that are the consensus endocytic signals recognized by a subset of FERM-domain containing sorting nexins.
source: Notably, the iRhom2 cytoplasmic tail contains two motifs, NxxY and NPxY (Figure 8—figure supplement 1B) that are the consensus endocytic signals recognized by a subset of FERM-domain containing sorting nexins, involved in endocytic recycling.
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge about sorting nexin recognition motifs.

claim: Preliminary experiments show that NxxY and NPxY motifs in iRhom2 appear not to be required for iTAP/iRhom2 binding.
source: However, our preliminary experiments in which we have mutated those motifs to alanines (AAAA), show that they appear not to be required for iTAP/iRhom2 binding (Figure 8—figure supplement 1C).
evidence: This is a finding from preliminary mutagenesis experiments shown in Figure 8—figure supplement 1C.

claim: Preliminary experiments detect no obvious colocalization of iTAP with early endosomes.
source: Moreover, although sorting nexins are intimately connected with the endocytic/recycling machinery, our preliminary experiments detect no obvious colocalization of iTAP with early endosomes (Figure 8—figure supplement 1D).
evidence: This is a finding from preliminary microscopy experiments shown in Figure 8—figure supplement 1D.

claim: PACS-2 binds directly to TACE.
source: It will also be interesting to reconcile the role of iTAP in the control of iRhom/TACE stability, versus that of PACS-2, which binds directly to TACE (Dombernowsky et al., 2015).
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge with citation support.

claim: TACE stimulants trigger detachment of TACE from iRhom2 on the cell surface.
source: This is relevant because TACE stimulants trigger detachment of TACE from iRhom2 on the cell surface (Grieve et al., 2017), a mechanism important for facilitating access of TACE to its substrates (Cavadas et al., 2017).
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge with citation support.

claim: The TNF and EGFR pathways are very stringently regulated by positive and negative feedback.
source: The TNF (and EGFR) pathway(s) are very stringently regulated by positive and negative feedback (Avraham and Yarden, 2011; Wallach, 2016; Vereecke et al., 2009).
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge with citation support.

claim: Preliminary experiments suggest that the phosphorylation of iRhom2 at residues required for the stimulation of TACE activity does not appear to influence iTAP binding.
source: Our preliminary experiments suggest that the phosphorylation of iRhom2 at residues required for the stimulation of TACE activity (Cavadas et al., 2017) does not appear to influence iTAP binding (data not shown), but future studies are required to investigate more widely the possibility of iTAP regulation by stimuli relevant to TACE biology.
evidence: This is a finding from preliminary experiments.

claim: Mature TACE levels are dramatically depleted in tissues from iTAP KO mice, including macrophages.
source: In addition to our extensive evidence indicating the requirement for iTAP for normal TACE function in human and mouse cells, we show that mature TACE levels are dramatically depleted in tissues from iTAP KO mice, including macrophages (Figure 7D).
evidence: This is a primary finding from western blot analysis shown in Figure 7D.

claim: ADAM17 homozygous mutant mice exhibit perinatal lethality.
source: Notably, whereas ADAM17 homozygous mutant mice exhibit perinatal lethality (Peschon et al., 1998), iTAP KO mice are born at near-normal mendelian ratios (Table 2), reach adulthood, appear superficially healthy and are fertile.
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge with citation support.

claim: iTAP KO mice are born at near-normal mendelian ratios.
source: Notably, whereas ADAM17 homozygous mutant mice exhibit perinatal lethality (Peschon et al., 1998), iTAP KO mice are born at near-normal mendelian ratios (Table 2), reach adulthood, appear superficially healthy and are fertile.
evidence: This is a finding from breeding experiments shown in Table 2.

claim: iTAP KO mice reach adulthood, appear superficially healthy and are fertile.
source: Notably, whereas ADAM17 homozygous mutant mice exhibit perinatal lethality (Peschon et al., 1998), iTAP KO mice are born at near-normal mendelian ratios (Table 2), reach adulthood, appear superficially healthy and are fertile.
evidence: This is a finding from observation of iTAP KO mice.

claim: Although loss of iTAP has a profound impact on the levels of mature TACE, the fraction remaining of mature TACE is sufficient to ensure normal mouse development.
source: These data indicate that although loss of iTAP indeed has a profound impact on the levels of mature TACE, the fraction remaining of mature TACE is sufficient to ensure normal mouse development.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the observation that iTAP KO mice are viable.

claim: ADAM17ex/ex mice were generated by the insertion of a new exon containing an in-frame stop codon, flanked by weak splice donor/acceptor sites inside the Adam17 (TACE) locus.
source: Several hypomorphic TACE mutant mice have been studied, including ADAM17ex/ex mice, which were generated by the insertion of a new exon containing an in-frame stop codon, flanked by weak splice donor/acceptor sites inside the Adam17 (TACE) locus (Chalaris et al., 2010).
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge with citation support.

claim: 95% of the TACE mRNA produced in ADAM17ex/ex mice contains the mutant exon, resulting in a dramatic reduction in TACE levels.
source: 95% of the TACE mRNA produced contains the mutant exon, resulting in a dramatic reduction in TACE levels (Chalaris et al., 2010).
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge with citation support.

claim: ADAM17ex/ex mice are born at normal mendelian ratios but are highly susceptible when challenged to an experimental model of colitis.
source: Notably, these animals are born at normal mendelian ratios but are highly susceptible when challenged to an experimental model of colitis (Chalaris et al., 2010).
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge with citation support.

claim: While traces of TACE can mitigate against lethality, they are not sufficient to prevent disease challenge.
source: This suggests that while traces of TACE can mitigate against lethality, they are not sufficient to prevent disease challenge.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the ADAM17ex/ex mouse data.

claim: Inhibiting TACE activity has been the subject of considerable pharmaceutical interest for decades.
source: Inhibiting TACE activity has been the subject of considerable pharmaceutical interest for decades, but attempts have failed, often because of cytotoxicity caused by unintended collateral targeting of ADAMs and matrix metalloproteases, that share active site architectures related to TACE (Murumkar et al., 2010).
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge with citation support.

claim: Attempts to inhibit TACE activity have failed, often because of cytotoxicity caused by unintended collateral targeting of ADAMs and matrix metalloproteases.
source: Inhibiting TACE activity has been the subject of considerable pharmaceutical interest for decades, but attempts have failed, often because of cytotoxicity caused by unintended collateral targeting of ADAMs and matrix metalloproteases, that share active site architectures related to TACE (Murumkar et al., 2010).
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge with citation support.

claim: iTAP has no apparent impact on other ADAMs.
source: As iTAP has no apparent impact on other ADAMs, the blockade of the iRhom:iTAP interaction may be an interesting potential therapeutic approach to attenuate TACE activity during disease.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the experimental findings.

claim: The blockade of the iRhom:iTAP interaction may be an interesting potential therapeutic approach to attenuate TACE activity during disease.
source: As iTAP has no apparent impact on other ADAMs, the blockade of the iRhom:iTAP interaction may be an interesting potential therapeutic approach to attenuate TACE activity during disease.
evidence: This is a speculative conclusion about potential therapeutic applications.

claim: At the organismal level, the impact of iTAP ablation is significantly less severe than the lethal phenotype of TACE KO mice.
source: Although iTAP ablation at the cellular level has a potent impact on TACE substrate cleavage, at the organismal level the impact is significantly less severe than the lethal phenotype of TACE KO mice (Peschon et al., 1998).
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from comparing iTAP KO and TACE KO mouse phenotypes.

claim: It may be possible to target iTAP to reduce TACE activity sufficiently to achieve a therapeutic impact in diseased tissues, without impinging on the normal physiological roles of TACE.
source: This implies that it may be possible to target iTAP to reduce TACE activity sufficiently to achieve a therapeutic impact in diseased tissues, without impinging on the normal physiological roles of TACE, which are sustained with minimal TACE levels in ADAM17ex/ex mutants (Chalaris et al., 2010) and presumably our iTAP KO mice.
evidence: This is a speculative conclusion about potential therapeutic applications.
